task.description: In this task you define and agree on the project scope, objectives, and approach. This task confirms that both consulting and the client have a clear understanding of the scope, objectives, and risks of the work to be undertaken before beginning.

template.note: PJM template with AIM Specific content

task.description: In this task you collect and compile all of the information including standards, policies, and procedures for project team members.

template.note: PJM template with AIM Specific content

task.description: In this task you determine, organize, estimate, link, and schedule all of the tasks representing the work to be performed on the project. This task can be performed with varying degrees of scope, rigor, and detail, depending on the circumstances.
In this task, you work closely with executive management on a strategy for improving the business and refining its business processes.
In this task, you compare the costs and benefits involved in making changes to the business processes and roles of the organization, as well as to the application.
In this task, you determine the data that needs to be collected during Business Process Architecture.
In this task, you examine the current business processes and practices to identify how the existing business system meets current business requirements.
In this task, you review which leading practices are relevant and appropriate for the organization.

In this task, you provide a general, high-level statement for each business process describing how the new process will operate. The statement determines any relevant principles that will regulate the operation of the new processes.
In this task, you produce high-level designs documenting how the new organization will operate after the applications are implemented.
In this task, you define the future business model in the form of integrated process flows built on the business processes supported by the new applications.
In this task, you document the procedures supporting the business processes enabled by the implementation of new applications.
In this task, the project team develops a complete picture of the organizations current financial and operating structure.
In this task, the project team examines current processes and practices to understand and document the main activities that keep the organization operating today.
In this task, you create the repository for key project findings and decisions that occur during the process and functional requirements gathering activities.
In this task, you research the current business volumes and estimate the future projected operational processing volumes, transaction patterns, and data storage volume requirements.
In this task, you define detailed business requirements and perform an initial assessment of application fit to these requirements.
In this task, you identify the high level requirements and policies that affect business and system security, control, and procedures.
In this task, you identify the business operating requirements that the operating functions and information systems functions agree are necessary to support the business processes.
In this task, you identify the organizations future reporting requirements
In this task, you will compare the process as envisioned in the Develop High-Level Designs (BP.070) with the processes supported by Oracle Applications.
In this task, you either install a new application, or prepare an existing application environment for detailed mapping activities.

template.description: Configured Mapping Environment Architecture and Configuration

task.description: In this task, you assess the fit of standard application and system features to detailed business requirements.
In this task, you map the data elements from the legacy system to the target application modules, business objects, and attributes.
In this task, you identify the new integration points that you require, based on your conceptual architecture and the mapping of the new applications onto the existing architecture.

In this task, you create an information view of the future business by specifying the future information usage and flow requirements across business functions, business organizations, applications, and data centers.
In this task, you will be required to analyze and map every reporting requirement to both a future business process and standard application report.
In this task, you perform an extended test of the business alternatives and validate integrated business processes based on the mapping decisions.
In this task, you secure approval for proposed business alternatives.
In this task, you capture the setup decisions and implement them in the appropriate environment.

template.description: Common Applications System Admin Application Setup
Work in Process Application Setup Document

task.description: In this task, you gather role and function information and relate them to application security and responsibilities. As business requirements are established and mapped to application features, you also begin to define the user security.
In this task, you identify the application and technical architecture requirements and strategy you will use for the design and development of the system you are implementing.

In this task, you identify the current application and technical architecture for the existing systems. This includes identifying existing applications, interfaces, databases, networks, and hardware platforms.

In this task, you identify possible candidate conceptual architectures for the new information systems you are implementing, and select the preferred architecture that best fits the overall needs of the business subject to the project constraints.

In this task, you design the functional architecture for the applications. This involves identifying those key setup parameters in the applications that are relevant to your particular implementation and establishing the values for those parameters.
In this task, you develop a strategy to provide the minimum level of systems availability that the business demands.

In this task, you analyze the reporting and information access requirements for the new business and specify at a high level how you will meet these in the new architecture. This is a systems view of the reporting and information access requirements.

In this task, you review information that you have gathered and analyzed since you created the initial draft of the Conceptual Architecture deliverable and incorporate any relevant new findings and decisions into the deliverable.

template.note: Update TA030_Preliminary_Conceptual_Architecture document created in TA.030

task.description: In this task, you design the application and database security architecture, incorporating the requirements generated by the business mapping process and the security requirements identified during the design of the conceptual architecture.

In this task, you design the new logical and physical architectures for the database tier and the application server tier. This task also defines the configuration for both the database and application tiers of the architecture.
In this task, you identify requirements for components or systems to support the architecture that were initially not identified within the project scope.

In this task, you plan the capacity for the new information systems at production cutover and for some prescribed period of future operations, allowing for business growth and any other known factors that could affect the system capacity requirements.

In this task, you define the physical platform and network configuration to support your final platform and network architecture. You map the physical application and database server architecture onto specific computing platforms.
In this task, you determine the details of the deployment of applications across data centers within the scope of the new architecture.
In this task, you identify any performance risks that are apparent based on the proposed architecture and suggest techniques to mitigate the risks.

In this task, you design the procedures and specify the tools that the client staff will need to manage the new system. After you design the procedures in this task, you need to test and refine them later in the project.
In this task, you prepare a strategy document that describes how your project responds to customization requests
In this task, when the approach to addressing a business issue determined during Map Business Requirements (BR.030) requires custom modules, you must estimate the effort required to complete them.
In this task, you define the standards that designers will follow when designing customizations.

task.description: In this task, you define the standards that developers follow to build customizations to the applications.

template.note: Use PJM.CR080_Acceptance_Certificate to generate Century Date Acceptance Certificate (see task description for additional information)

task.description: In this task, you document the functional features, use, and behavior of required customizations. The Application Extensions Functional Design confirms that you understand user requirements, and allows users to evaluate and approve the resulting features.

In this task you design the new database objects, such as tables, indexes, views and sequences required by the application extensions, and illustrate how the customizations integrate with the existing applications database schema.

template.note: Use PJM.CR080_Acceptance_Certificate to generate Century Date Acceptance Certificate (see task description for additional information)

task.description: In this task, you document the technical specifications for modifications, extensions, and configurable extensions.
In this task, you set up a design review meeting between business analysts, key users, technical analysts, and developers. The goal is to secure final acceptance of the complete designs.

template.note: Use PJM.CR080_Acceptance_Certificate to generate Century Date Acceptance Certificate (see task description for additional information)

task.description: In this task, you establish a platform and software environment that supports custom development.
In this task, you create new tables, indexes, views, grants, and synonyms to support custom module development.
In this task, you produce the modules to support customizations to the Applications. You also perform the first round of testing as part of this task.
In this task, you develop automated functions and detailed instructions to install customizations in the testing and production environments.

In this task, you define the scope of the conversion project, conversion objectives and approach, and prepare a strategy for converting information from the legacy systems to the new application environment.
In this task, you create the Conversion Standards that the conversion team will follow when performing conversion tasks.

template.note: Use PJM.CR080_Acceptance_Certificate to generate Century Date Acceptance Certificate (see task description for additional information)

task.description: In this task, you create the Conversion Environment, including the hardware platforms, servers and other software required to support the design and build activities of conversion.
In this task, you map the data elements from the legacy systems to the target Oracle Applications.
In this task, you define the plan to convert the business objects that require manual conversion.

template.note: Use PJM.CR080_Acceptance_Certificate to generate Century Date Acceptance Certificate (see task description for additional information)

task.description: In this task, you design and document the conversion programs.

template.note: Use PJM.CR080_Acceptance_Certificate to generate Century Date Acceptance Certificate (see task description for additional information)

task.description: In this task, you outline the testing plans for the unit, business object, and validation testing for conversion.

template.note: Use PJM.CR080_Acceptance_Certificate to generate Century Date Acceptance Certificate (see task description for additional information)

task.description: In this task, you create the conversion programs that perform all of the functions required to convert legacy business objects to the target Oracle Applications.

In this task, you test the conversion programs to verify that all programs work without errors and according to the conversion testing specifications pre-defined in the conversion unit testing components of the Conversion Test Plans (CV.070).

In this task, you test the complete conversion of each business object by executing all conversion modules for the business object in the appropriate sequence and verify that the resulting data is correct.
In this task, you validate that the target applications function correctly with the converted business objects.
In this task, you perform and document the installation of the conversion programs in the production environment.
In this task, you convert and migrate the production data from the old system to the new Oracle production environment.

In this task, you outline the overall requirements for creating documentation and specify the deliverables to be produced. You also identify the strategy you will use in publishing project-specific documentation.

In this task, you specify the standards for all documentation deliverables and determine the look and feel of the project documentation. In addition, you also specify the procedures that the team uses to develop documentation.
In this task, you document the definition of the terms that may be unfamiliar or confusing to project members.

In this task, you prepare a hardware and software environment that supports documentation development. You must procure, install, and test the environment. At the end of this task, you are ready to begin developing documentation.
In this task, you build and review a single prototype for each type of documentation deliverable. The result should be agreement on the look and feel of each documentation deliverable.
In this task, you gather material for the User Reference Manual and publish the final version. The User Reference Manual supplements the Oracle Applications user reference material.
In this task, you will publish a User Guide that defines a set of detailed procedures for using the applications.
In this task, you assemble the content of the Technical Reference Manual. The size of this task depends on the extent of the technical changes that were made to support the new applications.
In this task, you gather material for the System Management Guide and publish the final version. Perform this task in parallel with the execution of the business system test.
In this task, you identify the business system testing requirements and strategy you will use for the testing of the system you are implementing.
In this task, you develop the script to test individual application extension components. The tests validate that the application extension inputs, outputs, and processing logic function as designed.

In this task, you develop scripts to test modifications to standard Oracle Applications as well as new application extensions as part of a business flow. This will uncover any integration problems with other application extension components.

In this task, you develop the script to test the integration of application extensions with Oracle Applications modules. A system test script contains detailed steps which testers follow to verify the system setup and the integrity of custom application.
In this task, you develop the test script that validates the integration between your new application system and other third-party and legacy systems.
In this task, you install and configure one or more testing environments to support all testing activities.

In this task, you test application extension components on an individual basis to verify that the inputs, outputs, and processing logic of each application extension component functions without errors.

In this task, you test several application extension components together as part of a business flow to uncover any integration problems with other application extension components that provide or use the data manipulated by the target component.
In this task, you install application extensions in the system test environment to test the installation routines and refine them for the eventual production environment.
In this task, you provide basic training to key users participating in Business System Testing. A test environment is used to prepare key users for testing.

In this task, you test the integration of all business system flows within the target application system, including all standard and custom processes and reports. This task is equivalent to a full conference room pilot (CRP).
In this task, you test the system integration with other application systems in a production-like environment. The systems integration test is performed in a test environment.

template.description: Test Report for Systems Integration Test

task.description: In this task, you support users in performing their acceptance test of the new production system. The acceptance test is performed in a production environment.
In this task, you define the scope and objectives of performance testing in your project and outline the strategy that you will use to conduct the performance test.
In this task, you define the performance test scenarios that you wish to include in performance testing.
In this task, you define in more detail the sets of transactions that will execute during the performance test and the detailed transaction rate metrics for each transaction.

In this task, you define the detailed Performance Test Scripts for entering the data to perform online and batch transactions, inquiries, and reports that will model the processing occurring during a test scenario.
In this task, you design the performance test transaction programs that will execute the transactions, reports, and inquiries against the performance test environment.
In this task, you perform the detailed data design work for performance testing on the target environment.

task.deliverable: Performance Test Database Load Program Designs
task.description: In this task, you design the programs that will load test data into the performance test database.

template.description: Performance Test Database Load Program Designs

task.description: In this task, you create the special Performance Test Transaction Programs that will execute the transactions, reports, and inquiries against the performance test database.
In this task, you develop and test the programs that you will use to populate the performance test database with data.
In this task, you populate the Performance Test Database up to the full desired volume in preparation for subsequent migration of the database to the testing environment.
In this task, you prepare and document the separate environment where performance testing will take place.
In this task, you execute the performance test transaction programs against the test database and measure various performance metrics for individual transactions and system components.
In this task, you document the results and the description of performance testing in a format suitable for presentation to project managers, executive sponsors, and the project team.
In this task, you develop the organizational strategy for the project.
In this task, you orient the current project team members by communicating the project vision and charter, the rationale for key decisions, and presenting a high-level application overview.
In this task, you assess the learning requirements for the entire project team based on the project vision, charter, and scope in order to develop the learning paths aligned to project roles.

In this task, you establish the technical and physical infrastructure required for the actual project team learning, including either installing a new application environment or preparing an existing application environment.

In this task, you facilitate the learning events for the project team. These learning events cover tools, applications, and all knowledge and skills areas deemed necessary for the effective functioning of the team.
In this task, you conduct work sessions to assist business unit managers in understanding their roles towards making the project successful.

In this task, you generate key findings and recommendations toward the development of strategies that will help the organization become ready to use and accept the new technology and work expectations at production cutover.
In this task, you reach the stakeholder audiences with tailored messages at the optimal times and through the optimal media throughout the life of the project.
In this task, you conduct work sessions for middle and first-line managers, who are not on the project team, to assume their role in a successful people, process, and technology implementation.
In this task, you document the extent and the ramifications of the organizational change brought about by the new or improved business processes.
In this task, you define the human performance support systems requirements and execute the approach to meet the requirements to support the performance of users in their new roles.
In this task, you help transition the information technology groups to their new/updated mandate and roles, given the implementation of the new systems.
In this task, you gather insights on the learning needs of all audiences of users.
In this task, you create learning path approaches that allow users to become skilled in the new technologies, apply new/updated procedures, and fulfill their new roles.
In this task, you develop the learningware defined in the User Learning Plan (AP.140) to support the reskilling of employees.
In this task, you establish the technical and physical infrastructure required for the actual user learning, including preparing an environment that reflects the production applications environment.
In this task, you conduct the skills-change events developed in the User Learning Plan (AP.140), as well as track and document their progress.
In this task, you determine how well the production system, business and organizational performance meet the business objectives set at the beginning of the project.
In this task, you outline the business transition approach for migrating the system, organization, and people to production status.
In this task, you identify the operational infrastructure for managing and maintaining the application environment, servers, and network infrastructure in production.
In this task, you develop the detailed transition plan for moving onto the production system, as well as an implementation contingency plan.
In this task, you set up, configure, and install the database and application software for the production environment.
In this task, you implement the required setups in all of the applications as part of your configuration.

template.note: Complete Deliverable components from BR100 Application Setup

task.description: In this task, you activate the support personnel and procedures for the new business system and review requirements for support-related services from software suppliers, contractors, help desks, and other support services.
In this task, you formally verify that the organization’s systems, host facilities, local area networks (LANs), wide area networks (WANS), and people are prepared for production.
In this task, you confirm that organization-wide use of all aspects of the production system is in place.
In this task, you measure the performance of the system in the production environment.
In this task, you execute the system management procedures. This task is performed in perpetuity.
In this task, you solicit user feedback and act upon any requests relative to the implementation, production system, or support.
In this task, you involve the full analysis and execution of decommissioning former business systems.
In this task, you identify opportunities and challenges for the organization and propose a future business direction for the new implementation.

In this task, you identify innovations and advancements in software and technology that can enhance the efficiency, functionality, distributed nature, performance, and cost of maintaining the new production environment.
